newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hard left warn govt over confidence motion.
newsitem.headline: Italy hard left warn govt over confidence motion.

text.p: Italy's hard left Communist Refoundation said on Wednesday it would support the government in a future parliamentary confidence motion only if it stuck to basics and avoided detailed policy plans.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi said earlier he would put the fate of his government in the hands of President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro if his hard left allies decided to vote against the deployment of an Italian-led security force to Albania.

The Refoundation, which holds the balance of power in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), has pledged to oppose the Albanian mission and political commentators expect Scalfaro to order a confidence vote to establish Prodi's majority.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, leader of the centrist Italian Renewal party, said any confidence motion must be based on "precise issues and not general matters."
But Refoundation chairman Armando Cossutta rejected this. "If Prodi wants (to win) the confidence motion, then he should not enter into details," he told reporters.
"If we back the motion then we will vote for it with open hearts, If not then we will vote against."

Fabio Mussi, parliamentary leader of the largest coalition group, the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), said the government would soon have to reach an agreement with Refoundation over policy plans.
"The problem posed by Refoundation is quite large," he said, adding that one of the major issues which had to be confronted was the planned reform of the Welfare State.
